Closed-form root of the directed layer (C++ kernel)

Source: R/RcppExports.R
cpp_dag_closed_root.Rd

Solves the Pearson estimating equations of the modified Cholesky layer node by node: gamma_j = S[P_j, P_j]^-1 S[P_j, j] and delta_j = S[j, j] - S[j, P_j] gamma_j. A node with no parent keeps delta_j = S_jj and contributes no coefficient. Every delta_j is lifted to floor_rel * S_jj when it falls below that floor.

Usage

cpp_dag_closed_root(
  Shat,
  R,
  edge_idx,
  floor_rel = 1e-10,
  rcond_tol = 3.66685286250104e-11
)

Arguments

Shat

R x R sample covariance of the Pearson residuals, in the positional (elimination) order of the nodes.

R

integer number of responses.

edge_idx

integer |E| x 2 matrix of edges (i, j), i < j, 1-based, in positional order.

floor_rel

positivity floor of delta_j, relative to S_jj (to max |S_kk| when S_jj is not positive), so that it follows the scale of each response.

rcond_tol

a parent block S[P_j, P_j] whose equilibrated form D^-1 S[P_j, P_j] D^-1, D = diag(S[P_j, P_j])^(1/2), has a reciprocal condition number not above this tolerance is near singular: its coefficients are not identified and are taken from a solve with a ridge of 1e-8 on the unit diagonal of the equilibrated block.

Value

list with gamma (one per edge, in the order of edge_idx), delta (length R), the number of nodes whose normal equations needed a ridge, the number of innovation variances lifted to the positivity floor, and ill_conditioned, the positional (1-based) nodes whose parent block is near singular.
